subject: Private hosting: ownership split + budget exception canvas
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace OConnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private hosting: ownership split + budget exception canvas

Team —

Bringing this thread together to capture a concise decision canvas for SummitCare's request for a VPC/on-prem option. They want a hard isolation lane with an SLA that mirrors Dedicated, but they're asking for a one-off integration budget and exception to staged staffing assumptions.

Can each of you weigh in on the specific asks below by EOD Wednesday so I can prep a one-page for leadership:

- Scope: SummitCare wants private control plane + isolated GPU pool in their Azure tenancy for pilot (3 months). Is this 'Private (VPC)' or 'on-prem appliance' from our side?
- Ownership split: who owns day-zero network setup (Redwood infra team vs. SummitCare network)?
- Budget exception: they asked for a $65k integration budget (engineering + security review). Recommend approve/decline and alternate proposals.
- Risk: 3 quick bullets of operational risk that would require leadership signoff.

I attached the draft cost estimate and an early control matrix — take whatever rows are relevant.

Thanks — short replies appreciated.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships (interim)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: isolation-cost-estimate-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), privatedeploy-control-matrix.pdf (PDF)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Grace OConnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting: ownership split + budget exception canvas

Vivek —

Quick technical take: this is a VPC-hosted private control plane (not on-prem appliance) unless the customer insists on air-gapped hardware. For the pilot you described (3 months, Azure tenancy), our responsibilities should be:

- Redwood: control plane provisioning, model runtime image, runtime config (autoscaling limits, quantization profile), certs for service endpoints, basic rollout policy.
- Customer (SummitCare): network peering, NSGs, private endpoint configuration, routing to their subnet, AAD/integration.

Staffing/budget: $65k is reasonable for an accelerated pilot if it buys: 2 SRE engineer-weeks (networking + runtime), 1 security engineer week (compliance checklist), plus project management and runbook packaging. If leadership wants to protect runway, propose a $40k base + $25k contingency tied to scope growth (e.g., additional model variants or higher SLA).

Operational risks (short):
1) Network misconfig -> production traffic leakage (mitigate with e2e dry run + packet filters).
2) Runtime version drift -> substitute automated image pinning and a canary deployment.
3) Support latency -> pilot requires 24h on-call by Redwood SRE (or we accept slower SLA).

I flagged the runtime dependencies in the attached estimate (tab: runtime-costs). Happy to sync if you want to change the split.

— Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Architecture

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace OConnor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting: ownership split + budget exception canvas

Adding the product/ops lens:

Summary recommendation (for the one-pager):
- Approve pilot with conditional funding: $40k base integration fee + milestone-triggered $25k (gate: successful endpoint privacy test + runbook acceptance).
- Ownership: Redwood owns the control plane and runtime images; SummitCare owns network setup and IAM.
- Support: Redwood provides weekend-lite coverage for pilot; full 24/7 on-call only after paid SLA upgrade.

Product asks / roadmap implications (short):
- We need a minimal isolated onboarding flow (documented runbook + templated ARM deployment) — estimate 3 dev-weeks to build and 1 doc week. That should be part of the integration budget or listed as separate product investment.
- Prioritize a small UI toggle in Console for 'private pilot' metadata so billing/observability pipelines tag traffic properly (1 sprint frontend + 1 sprint backend).

Risks / exceptions to highlight:
- If SummitCare requires encryption-at-rest BYOK in their HSM, that's an additional compliance/ops cadence and will add ~2 weeks and ~$12k of effort.

I'll draft the one-pager language after we finalize numbers — flagging the ARM template requirement as a potential product ask against roadmap.

— Stephanie
VP, Product
From: Caroline Park <caroline@summitcare.io>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private hosting: ownership split + budget exception canvas

Thanks all — this is really helpful and aligns with our internal constraints. A couple quick clarifications from SummitCare: 

- We can own the network peering and AAD integration; we do need Redwood to manage certs and runtime images end-to-end.
- The proposed $40k + $25k milestone spread works for procurement, but we need an invoice milestone schedule (PO needed by May 10).
- We may require BYOK for a limited set of keys — please confirm the $12k estimate and timing.

Next steps: Vivek, if you can send the one-pager and a compact SOW + milestone invoice schedule, procurement will be ready to circulate internally. Happy to join a 30m sync if useful.

Best,
Caroline Park
Head of IT Integration
SummitCare
